body:
This is interesting. Looking at https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1071, you noted that release export is optimized for speed and does *less* checks, which is why we are now seeing errors surface differently here. An uncaught "soft" error / state check that *would* be caught in debug export could lead to a "hard" error elsewhere in release export (essentially undefined behavior).

Optimizing release exports for speed has its merrits and I imagine Godot has been developing with this philosophy in mind. Thus we could be seeing similar behavior differences between debug and release exports elsewhere, most interactions which may not be documented yet.

So I'd lean to us adding checks as they show up and where it makes sense and it seems you are also leaning for this instance to be properly caught consistently. I think specifically for this instance, release export should stop and "hard" error at the validation that would be caught in debug export. Debug export seems to be catching a real error that should not be allowed to continue, even on release export.

Sure we lose out on some speed because of this change on release export, but I think the DX improvement far outweighs the loss.

Wdyt?
